summary: This legacy internal IT helpdesk ticketing application (Django 1.4 / Python 2.7) is not suitable for AI agent integration in its current state. It lacks machine-readable API interfaces, has critical security vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XSS), no authentication enforcement on endpoints, no idempotency guarantees, no human-in-the-loop controls, and zero observability infrastructure.

findings.finding: No machine-readable API exists (no REST, GraphQL, or RPC endpoints with structured responses)
Views return rendered HTML templates or raw HTML strings — no JSON/structured data output
No API schema or contract (no OpenAPI/Swagger, no WSDL, no documentation of request/response formats)
No versioned API — endpoints are Django view functions with no version prefix or content negotiation
No input validation or schema enforcement — query parameters are consumed directly without type checking
No authentication enforced on any endpoint — views lack @login_required or permission checks
No support for machine identity (no API keys, OAuth tokens, service accounts, or mTLS)
SQL injection in both views allows full database access bypass regardless of any intended access controls
Session-based auth only (cookie-based) — unsuitable for programmatic agent access without browser emulation
SECRET_KEY committed to source control — session tokens and CSRF tokens can be forged
AuthenticationMiddleware is loaded but not utilized by any view
No idempotency controls — repeated identical requests may produce different results depending on database state
SQL injection allows arbitrary state mutation (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP) via GET requests
All operations use GET method — no proper HTTP method semantics (no distinction between safe/unsafe operations)
No transaction isolation guarantees — raw cursor queries with no explicit transaction management
Single PostgreSQL instance with no replication — single point of failure for all state
No caching layer — every request hits the database directly
Database credentials are hardcoded plaintext in source control
No approval workflows, confirmation steps, or review gates exist anywhere in the application
No rate limiting or throttling — an agent could issue unlimited requests
No undo/rollback capability exposed to users or systems
No audit trail — actions are not logged with actor identity or timestamp
No escalation paths — no mechanism to flag an action for human review
No webhook or callback mechanism for asynchronous human approval
No structured logging — only a single print statement exists in the entire codebase
No metrics collection (no Prometheus, CloudWatch, StatsD, or equivalent)
No distributed tracing (no correlation IDs, no X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry)
No health check endpoint — impossible to determine system availability programmatically
DEBUG = True leaks full stack traces to end users but provides no operational visibility
No alerting beyond Django's default email-on-500 to a single internal address
No request logging (no access logs beyond Apache's default)

remediationPriorities: Upgrade runtime — Migrate to supported Python 3.x and Django 4.x+ to receive security patches and modern framework features.
Fix critical security vulnerabilities — Eliminate SQL injection (use parameterized queries/ORM), fix XSS (use template engine), externalize secrets, disable DEBUG in production.
Add a machine-readable API layer — Implement a RESTful JSON API (e.g., Django REST Framework) with OpenAPI schema documentation.
Implement proper authentication — Add API key or OAuth2 client-credentials support for machine callers alongside session auth for humans.
Add idempotency controls — Use proper HTTP methods (POST for creation with idempotency keys, PUT for updates), add ETags for concurrency control.
Implement observability — Add structured logging, request tracing (correlation IDs), metrics, and a health check endpoint.
Add human-in-the-loop controls — Implement rate limiting, action audit logging, and approval workflows for destructive operations.
Add API documentation and contracts — Publish and maintain an OpenAPI specification as the agent integration contract.
